w10_T4_003658: Ravi had 84 sports cards, more than his friend Deepak's dozen or so. He traded for 76 more cards at school. He then lost 1 card that slipped out of his backpack. A dealer's promotion multiplied his collection fivefold. He split the whole collection evenly three ways with two cousins, keeping only his own third. His uncle then gave him 31 more cards, and a school fair added 56 more. How many cards did Ravi have at the end?
w10_T4_003659: In the morning, a bookstore had 75 novels on the bargain table, while a completely different table nearby held 300 cookbooks. By midday, 23 novels sold. In the afternoon, a publisher's promotion tripled the remaining novels on that table. By evening, 4 novels were pulled for being damaged. Late that evening, a final donation of 73 novels was added. How many novels were on the bargain table by the end of the evening?
w10_T4_003668: A toy store had 236 puzzles in stock, while a completely separate display held 900 board games. A weekend sale sold 57 puzzles. A shipment delay then caused 102 more puzzles to be sent back to the supplier by mistake. A correction shipment brought 68 puzzles back. Finally, a holiday order multiplied the puzzle stock ninefold. How many puzzles were in stock after the holiday order?
w10_T4_003670: In the morning, a print shop had 165 flyers ready for a campaign. By midday, 7 flyers were damaged and thrown out. In the afternoon, a rush reprint multiplied the flyer stock sevenfold. By evening, 82 flyers were handed out at a street fair. Overnight, the remaining flyers were split evenly among four volunteers for the next day's distribution, and this story follows only one volunteer's stack. How many flyers did that volunteer have?
w10_T4_003673: Grace had 110 dollars saved, more than her brother Sam's 30. She earned 53 more dollars babysitting. She then spent 156 dollars on a new phone case and screen protector bundle. A refund program tripled whatever cash she had left. A final bonus from her part-time job multiplied it eightfold. How much money did Grace have in the end?
w10_T4_003675: In the morning, a farm had 61 chickens, while a dozen ducks waddled around in a separate pen. By midday, 41 more chicks hatched. In the afternoon, a fox got into the coop and 12 chickens went missing, even though the farmer's log also mentioned an unrelated 500 turkeys on a neighboring farm. By evening, a trade with another farmer added 49 chickens. Overnight, a breeding boom multiplied the flock sevenfold. The next morning, a disease outbreak led to a loss of 356 chickens. Finally, a matching restock from the county multiplied the flock eightfold. How many chickens were on the farm after the restock?
w10_T4_003679: A tech recycler had 167 old phones dropped off, while a dozen broken tablets sat in an unrelated bin. A bulk pickup multiplied the phone count fourfold. A second pickup multiplied it ninefold again. A school donation drive added 77 more phones. Finally, 601 phones were shipped out for refurbishing. How many phones were left at the recycler?
w10_T4_003688: Ben had 182 marbles, more than his classmate Theo's 65. He won 54 more marbles in a game, even though a completely different tournament across town gave away 1,000 marbles as a grand prize. He then lost 122 marbles in a rough game of ringer. A marble-multiplying machine at the fair multiplied his remaining stash sevenfold. His cousin gave him 10 more, and he found 25 more under his bed. How many marbles did Ben end up with?
w10_T4_003693: A school garden had 28 tomato plants, plus a dozen unrelated pepper plants in a different bed. A seed-sharing program multiplied the tomato plants sevenfold. A late frost killed 4 of them. A community donation added 50 more plants. A second growing season multiplied the plants sevenfold again. Finally, a neighbor donated 9 more plants. How many tomato plants were in the garden by the end?
w10_T4_003695: Camille had 223 dollars in her account, or 22,300 cents as her little brother liked to calculate, more than her cousin Theo's 90 dollars. She paid 69 dollars for a textbook and 39 dollars for a bus pass. A refund then added 23 dollars, and a part-time job paycheck brought in 78 more. Finally, a matching bonus from her bank multiplied her balance fourfold. How much money did Camille have after the bonus?
w10_T4_003699: In the morning, a factory had 85 units of a component ready, while an unrelated production line had made 500 different parts overnight. By midday, a bulk order multiplied the component count ninefold. In the afternoon, a supplier delivered 48 more units. By evening, three separate matching contracts each multiplied the stock again, fourfold, then fivefold, then threefold, in that order. How many units were in stock by the end of the evening?
w10_T4_003700: A charity 5K had 161 registered runners, while a completely separate marathon across the state had 2,000 registrants. A last-minute sponsorship multiplied the registration ninefold. A wave of 781 cancellations then came in due to a weather warning. A late sign-up period added 37 more runners, and a partner club brought in 35 more. A final review removed 220 duplicate registrations. The organizers then split the remaining runners evenly into five starting waves, and this story follows only the first wave. How many runners were in the first wave?
w10_T4_003707: In the morning, Leo had 101 dollars saved, or 10,100 cents as his sister liked to point out, more than his friend Marco's 40 dollars. Over the course of the day, four separate matching bonuses hit his account in turn: one multiplied it sevenfold in the morning, another multiplied it sevenfold again by midday, a third multiplied it threefold in the afternoon, and a fourth multiplied it sixfold by evening. That night, he paid 7,560 dollars for a used car. How much money did Leo have left after buying the car?
w10_T4_003713: In the morning, a warehouse had 138 dollars worth of returned deposit bottles, or 13,800 cents as the recycling center's receipt listed it. By midday, a delivery added 60 more dollars in bottle deposits. In the afternoon, 140 dollars was paid out to a hauler. That afternoon, three back-to-back matching rebates multiplied the total in turn, doubling it, then multiplying it eightfold, then sixfold. By evening, a final 80-dollar rebate was added. How much money was in the account by evening?
w10_T4_003715: A stadium sold 60 season tickets on the first day of a pre-sale, while a rival team's stadium across town sold 800 tickets that same day. A social-media push multiplied ticket sales ninefold. A second wave multiplied it fivefold again. Half of those tickets were then set aside for a different section, and this story follows only the tickets that stayed in the main section. A final rush multiplied the main-section tickets ninefold. Finally, 49 more tickets were added from a corporate block. How many tickets were sold in the main section?
w10_T4_003719: A fish tank held 147 liters of water, or about 38.8 gallons as the pet store's tag noted, while a separate display tank held 900 liters. A leak drained 96 liters overnight. The next day, a maintenance flush removed 22 more liters. A refill then added 40 liters back. A second small leak lost 7 more liters. Finally, staff multiplied the tank's water sevenfold by connecting it to a larger reservoir for a special exhibit. How many liters of water were in the tank after the exhibit setup?
w10_T4_003721: In the morning, a warehouse had 84 crates of soda. By midday, a supplier's rush order multiplied the crates sevenfold. In the afternoon, 209 crates were shipped out to a grocery chain. By evening, a returning delivery brought back 66 crates. Overnight, a matching bulk order multiplied the remaining crates sevenfold again. How many crates were in the warehouse the next morning?
w10_T4_003722: A toy factory produced 145 action figures on the first day of a run. The next day, workers added 9 more, and a third day added 50 more. A bulk order then multiplied the total eightfold. A second matching bulk order multiplied it fivefold again. The whole batch was then split evenly among five distributors, and this story follows only one distributor's share. That distributor further divided their share evenly among four stores, and only one store's shipment continued. How many action figures did that store receive?
w10_T4_003724: A blood bank had 207 pints in storage, or about 25.9 gallons as the coordinator's report converted it, while a dozen empty collection bags sat in a supply closet. A morning donor added 7 more pints. A hospital order used up 154 pints. A company blood drive brought in 16 more, and a college drive added 64 more. A quality check then removed 2 contaminated pints. Finally, a regional partnership multiplied the remaining pints fourfold by combining stock from three sister banks. How many pints were in storage after the partnership consolidation?
w10_T4_003744: Oliver had 103 dollars, or 10,300 cents as his little cousin liked to calculate, more than his neighbor Felix's 40 dollars. A weekend job doubled his savings. He then spent 11 dollars on lunch. A refund added 59 dollars, and he later paid 129 dollars toward a new bike. How much money did Oliver have left?
w10_T4_003745: A toy warehouse had 84 crates of building blocks, exactly seven dozen crates delivered over a shift that ran 180 minutes, or three hours. A supplier delivery added 68 more crates. A bulk-order multiplier then quadrupled the crate count for a big retail contract. A second delivery added 60 more crates. Another matching contract quadrupled the count again. A quality check then removed 40 damaged crates. Finally, a massive shipment of 1,441 crates went out to fulfill the retail order. How many crates were left in the warehouse?
w10_T4_003753: In the morning, a warehouse had 188 boxes of holiday cards, or about 7,520 cards if you count 40 to a box as the packing slip notes. By midday, a matching shipment multiplied the box count fivefold. In the afternoon, 527 boxes were shipped to retailers. Later that afternoon, another 347 boxes went out on a second truck. By evening, a return brought back 21 boxes. Overnight, the remaining boxes were split evenly among three regional hubs, and this story follows only one hub. How many boxes did that hub receive?
w10_T4_003755: Nadia had 64 dollars saved, more than her brother Kofi's 20, even though a completely separate account of hers held an unrelated 500 dollars in savings bonds. A weekend job tripled her cash. A holiday bonus doubled it again. She then split the total evenly among four envelopes, keeping only the first envelope's share. A matching grant multiplied that envelope's contents fivefold, and a final store credit doubled it once more. How much money was in the first envelope at the end?
w10_T4_003756: Yuki had 211 origami cranes, more than her classmate Sana's 90. She gave away 107 cranes to a hospital ward. A folding party then multiplied her remaining cranes fourfold. Afterward, 9 cranes were damaged and discarded. She gave 31 more to a school fundraiser. Finally, a friend gave her 19 more cranes. How many cranes did Yuki have left?
w10_T4_003758: A charity had 231 dollars in its account, or 23,100 cents as the treasurer liked to joke. A bake sale added 18 more dollars. Then 63 dollars was spent on supplies for the next event. A matching corporate donor multiplied the account eightfold. Finally, the charity paid 451 dollars for a venue deposit. How much money was left in the account?
